## Graco Experts Share Liquid Finishing Essentials at FABTECH


As manufacturers work to improve finish consistency and throughput and reduce material waste, rework and operating costs, selecting the right finishing equipment for the job has become increasingly important.


At FABTECH, North America’s largest metal forming, fabricating, welding and finishing event, Graco experts shared guidance to help manufacturers navigate important decisions within liquid finishing applications.


One of the educational sessions, presented by Michelle Striggow, category sales manager; Wendy Hartley, senior product manager; and Blake Erickson, senior product manager, addressed a current manufacturing challenge: selecting the right technology for finish quality, production demands and material efficiency.


The sessions highlighted essential liquid finishing information and focused on how equipment selection should start with the application itself instead of the technology.


*Wendy Hartley, senior product manager (left); Blake Erickson, senior product manager (middle); and Michelle Striggow, category sales manager (right)*


#### Start with the application requirements


Every liquid finishing application is different and may require different equipment.


During the sessions, a three-step framework was outlined that manufacturers can use when evaluating a finishing system:


1. Define the application and process.
2. Understand transfer efficiency.
3. Select the appropriate spray technology.


#### Define the liquid finishing application and process


Before comparing different spray technologies, manufacturers should first understand the characteristics of the material being applied. Material properties can directly affect the specific delivery system, pressure requirements, applicator and operating procedures needed.


Key material characteristics to consider include:


- Coating type and chemistry
-


Solventborne or waterborne materials


-


One-component or two-component coatings


-


Viscosity


-


Moisture or shear sensitivity


-


Appearance-critical finishes or protective coatings


Once the material requirements are defined, manufacturers should evaluate production and facility considerations, such as:


-


Manual or automatic application


-


Production volume and throughput requirements


-


Part size and shape


-


Number of operators and applicators


-


New process implementation or expansion of an existing line


-


Booth-side systems or centralized paint kitchens


-


Pneumatic or electric power requirements


-


Circulation and filtration needs


-


Available installation space


Determining these variables early helps manufacturers narrow down equipment options and identify the ones that best support their production needs.


#### Why transfer efficiency matters


Transfer efficiency is receiving increased attention across manufacturing operations because it impacts material use, finish quality and operating costs. Higher transfer efficiency can help reduce overspray and reduce waste and disposal and maintenance costs.


However, achieving full transfer efficiency requires more than selecting the right spray gun. Several factors determine the actual performance of spray guns, including:


-


Air and fluid pressure


-


Fluid flow and tip size


-


Gun setup


-


Booth airflow


-


Part size and shape


-


Operator technique


-


Paint resistivity and grounding (applicable to electrostatic applications)


Understanding these factors can help manufacturers maximize transfer efficiency and deliver consistent results in their production process.


#### Match the technology to the production goal


Different spray technology offer different results and advantages, making it important for manufacturers to select technology based on application requirements and production needs.


**Air spray technology**


Air spray technology creates atomization when a low-speed fluid stream meets high-speed air. Manufacturers can adjust fluid and air flow to achieve specific material consistency and application requirements.


Conventional, HVLP and compliant/LVMP technologies each offer different balances of finish quality, production speed and transfer efficiency.


[Learn more about air spray technology.](https://www.graco.com/us/en/in-plant-manufacturing/products/liquid-coating/spray-booth/spray-guns-applicators/air-spray-guns.html)


**Airless spray technology**


Airless spray technology uses hydraulic force to push material through an orifice, creating atomization as the coating exits the tip and encounters the surrounding air. This technology requires higher pressure and provides a fast and heavy spray finish.


[Learn more about airless spray guns.](https://www.graco.com/us/en/in-plant-manufacturing/products/liquid-coating/spray-booth/spray-guns-applicators/airless-spray-guns.html)


**Air-assisted airless spray technology**


Air-assisted technology combines hydraulic force with air assistance to create finer atomization compared to traditional airless spray technology, resulting in finer finish results and more performance.


[Learn more about air-assisted airless spray guns.](https://www.graco.com/us/en/in-plant-manufacturing/products/liquid-coating/spray-booth/spray-guns-applicators/air-assisted-airless-spray-guns.html)


**Electrostatic spray technology**


Electrostatic technology uses charged coating particles to improve material coverage, as the charge attracts the material to grounded parts. This attraction helps provide consistent results and improves transfer efficiency. Proper grounding is important for this technology for both safety and performance.


[Learn more about electrostatic spray guns.](https://www.graco.com/us/en/in-plant-manufacturing/products/liquid-coating/spray-booth/spray-guns-applicators/electrostatic-paint-spray-guns.html)


#### Better equipment selection starts with a better understanding of the application


When manufacturers understand their material, its requirements and production needs, they can make more informed decisions and build finishing systems that support the quality, efficiency and performance they need.


Graco offers a wide selection of liquid finishing technologies designed to help manufacturers improve finish consistency and throughput and reduce material waste.[Explore Graco’s full line of liquid finishing equipment](https://www.graco.com/us/en/in-plant-manufacturing/products/liquid-coating.html) .
